newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians round up 125 illegal immigrants in south.
newsitem.headline: Italians round up 125 illegal immigrants in south.

text.p: Italian police rounded up a total of 125 people in several groups who tried to enter southern parts of the country illegally by boat.

In a separate incident, investigators in the southern town of Taranto announced the arrest of 10 men charged with criminal association in connection with allegations that they had arranged for Albanians to bring marijuana into Italy in exchange for a promise of paperwork entitling them to work in this country.
Three of those arrested were Italians and seven were from former Yugoslavia, police said.
Seventy-four would-be immigrants -- from Albania, Turkey, Egypt and Montenegro -- were stopped along the coast of Puglia, just across the Adriatic from Albania, early on Monday, police said.
Fifty-one North Africans were stopped on the small island of Pantelleria, between Sicily and Tunisia, after they were dropped off by a motorboat, which was chased by Italian coast guard but escaped.
Immigration officials said all 125 would be served with expulsion orders.

The southern Adriatic coast and another remote island between Sicily and North Africa, Lampedusa, are favoured entry points. Authorities acknowledge that many of illegal immigrants ignore the expulsion notices and stay in Italy or try to move on to other European countries.
